Man Buys New 2027 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X Coupe for $253,320, Now Wants More Than $278,000 for It
23 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
I guess we shouldn't be that surprised about what just happened here. Someone bought this ZR1X for $253,200 and then pretty much immediately listed it for sale at auction, but then refused to part with it despite the highest bid coming in at way over MSRP. The bidding stopped at $278,000, which fell short of the reserve.
So, what's the problem? Well, $25,000 over MSRP is not enough in today's market to land you a still-new ZR1X. This is the hottest C8 Corvette money can buy and these are still fetching nearly $100,000 over MSRP easily. Just recently, a Red Mist example with 1,200 miles on the clock sold for $315,000, which came in at roughly $60,000 over MSRP. And that's the cheapest used ZR1X pretty much anywhere.
Yes, this Arctic White example does have way fewer miles, and while the spec is a bit different, I can still understand why the seller would hold out for more. Perhaps closer to $300,000. Give or take.
At the same time, I also understand why someone would try to land it "on the cheap". It's how you force the market to adjust, and had this sold for only $25,000 over MSRP, it would have changed the ZR1X "landscape" drastically. But people aren't ready for that just yet. Valuations closer to MSRP are coming for the flagship C8, but they're coming sometime next year. Definitely not now.
Anyway, time to take a closer look at the spec on this car, starting with the exterior. Highlights include the removable carbon-fiber roof panel, a rear spoiler, carbon fiber accents, LED headlights, front and rear cameras, plus a set of Carbon Flash 20" and 21" forged wheels wearing Michelin rubber. There's also a front-axle lift system, which is a must in pretty much any supercar - especially one that's been fitted with lower body aero elements.
Meanwhile, inside is where you'll find the Jet Black leather GT2 bucket seats (heated/ventilate), the Stealth Interior Trim Package, carbon fiber trim, a keyless entry system, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a Bose sound system, sat-nav, a head-up display, and a heated and leather-trimmed steering wheel. In terms of electronic driver aids, you've got lane-keep assist, rear cross-traffic alert, side blind-zone alert, and forward collision alert.
Photo: Bring a Trailer As for the drivetrain, it's as good as it gets by modern-day standards. There's a twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter LT7 V8 unit, working alongside an electric motor and a 1.9-kWh liquid-cooled lithium-ion battery pack. Altogether, they "Voltron" into a 1,250-horsepower monstrosity, which also produces 973 lb-ft (1,320 Nm) of torque. Everything gets sent to all four wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic and an electronic AWD system.
In a straight line, the Corvette ZR1X can rocket to 60 mph (97 kph) in just under 2 seconds flat (with a 1-foot rollout), and if you're doing everything perfectly, you might just put up an 8.67-second quarter mile time. Good luck.
